prior_information: Two previously published scientific hashes differ; published comparison reports 1299 float differences with maximum absolute difference 3.608224830031759e-16. This is known prior evidence, not a blind study.

factor.name: ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY
factor.purpose: Test whether changing ATen CPU dispatch alone changes the complete scientific output on this host. This does not control all BLAS or oneDNN dispatch.

controls: fresh isolated interpreter for every sample
same allow-listed environment controls except ATEN_CPU_CAPABILITY

acceptance.strict_scientific_hash: Report SHA-256 equality independently. Never redefine or round scientific output.
acceptance.exact: JSON types, keys, array length/order; schema, data identity, protocol and all config floats; strings/bools/null/integers; predictions, row IDs, confusion matrices, selected architecture, checks; count-derived accuracy, precision, recall, f1, macro_f1 and their summaries; every float outside the explicit continuous-output allowlist. Training priors are count-derived and exact.
acceptance.numeric: Finite IEEE-754 binary64 only. At most 8 representable steps (ULP distance) for allow-listed continuous floats; no nonzero absolute floor. Signed zeros numeric-equal, strict hash still distinguishes their JSON encoding.
acceptance.rationale: Eight adjacent finite binary64 representable steps is an explicitly chosen tight diagnostic budget. ULP distance counts representable numbers, not differing mantissa bits. It is intentionally stringent and is not a derived error guarantee for matrix products, transcendental functions or iterative training. No threshold will be changed after outcomes are observed. Numeric failure remains failure and a subject for further investigation.
acceptance.invalid: Nonfinite numbers, duplicate object keys, malformed Wine schema/identity or failed protocol checks reject comparison.
acceptance.outcome: Preserve exact hash status, exact-field status, numeric status, counts/maxima/paths, full raw outputs and failures separately. No probability rounding or model/seed/test tuning.

stop: Four successful full-workload captures; fail with preserved evidence on worker/config errors or changed controls. If dispatch is not observably different, mark intervention ineffective rather than infer no numerical effect. No search for a passing factor or threshold.
limits: Shared-host timing is descriptive only; no speed claim
No inference about earlier CI hosts without their CPU metadata
No attribution of individual kernel or earlier cross-run mismatch cause
No cross-platform or general error-bound claim
